topic: Agent-Doctor: Local-First Observability, Cost Analysis and Project Memory

key_points: Local-first observability for Claude Code without wrappers, SDKs, or cloud dependencies
Real-time cost tracking, tool latency, and subagent visibility while session is live
Shows per-subagent cost breakdown (main $1.82/89 calls, executor $0.41/31 calls, verifier $0.24/22 calls)
Zero telemetry, Apache 2.0, Node >=18, runs on localhost:4999
Solves the problem that Claude JSONL transcripts are not usable in real time — you only notice budget burn after the fact
Local-first observability that routes what it sees back into the agent's next turn (hooks, MCP tools, anomaly detection)
Agent learns from its own failures — injects fix path into next prompt when an Edit fails 3 times or a build keeps breaking
Detects stale in-memory copies vs on-disk state (e.g. re-read auth.go before next edit)
Monolith in the agent's loop, silent until it talks back
Open-source AI prompt and agent workflow analyzer that finds token waste, repeated context, and prompt caching opportunities
Reduces LLM cost and latency by surfacing caching opportunities
Local-first cost tracking proxy for LLM APIs
Free, local, open-source LLM cost analyzer — see where your LLM bill leaks, on your machine
Finds which LLM calls a cheaper model could handle (local, MIT)
67 HN points — strong community interest in local cost analysis
Free, local tool to track AI coding token usage and cost across 37 tools and agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini)
Breakdown by model, project, and task
112 HN points — high demand for per-task token/cost attribution
Local-first analytics dashboard for Claude Code — usage, costs, sessions, projects
No cloud, no telemetry, just your data
Emphasizes privacy as a differentiator
Tool-agnostic project context in plain markdown — works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini
Stops re-explaining your project every AI session
Plain markdown = portable, human-readable project memory

stats.fact: ObservAgent demo shows a single Claude Code session burning $2.47 total across 142 tool calls, with per-subagent cost attribution (main $1.82, executor $0.41, verifier $0.24).
CodeBurn (local token/cost tracker) supports 37 tools and agents including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Gemini, and drew 112 HN points on launch.
Frugon, a local MIT-licensed LLM cost analyzer that finds which calls a cheaper model could handle, drew 67 HN points.
ObservAgent reports ~50 MB memory baseline, <50 ms query latency, and 5K events/second throughput for local agent observability.
Claude Code writes JSONL transcripts of sessions, but they are not usable in real time — cost overruns are only discovered after the budget is already burned.

angles: Local-first observability as a privacy/sovereignty differentiator — no cloud, no telemetry, data stays on your machine
Real-time cost attribution per subagent/tool/model vs. post-hoc JSONL analysis that is too late to act on
Project memory as a cost lever: re-explaining context every session wastes tokens; persistent memory cuts repeated-context spend
The 'agent learns from its own failures' loop — observability that feeds back into the next turn rather than a postmortem
Open-source vs. commercial observability tradeoffs for solo developers and small teams
Token waste detection and prompt-caching opportunities as a concrete cost-reduction play
